text.p: Gaming machine maker Aristocrat Leisure Ltd said on Tuesday it was on target to meet its prospectus forecasts for profits in the 1996/97 financial year.
"We are still on track to meet prospectus forecasts for 1997," managing director John Dougal told reporters.
Aristocrat forecast earnings before tax and abnormals of A$32.8 million for the 1996/97 year to June 30 when it floated on the Australian Stock Exchange in July 1996.

Dougall said sales in the states of Queensland and Victoria were likely to be slower than forecast as well sales to Turkey due to the change in government there last year but New South Wales was likely to be a bit stronger.
"We are still going to achieve the numbers set but it might just be a different mix," he said.
In its float prospectus, Aristocrat forecast its sales would rise to A$321 million in 1996/97 from an actual A$256.92 million in 1995/96.
